cards.lore: You're just a Complete Monster with a better PR team and a highly marketable tragic backstory.
cards.power: Steal audience sympathy while doing the exact same job as the villain.

cards.lore: A narrative shortcut for lazy authors who need you to stop thinking and start blindly booing.
cards.power: Absorb all audience hatred to instantly shield the writers from having to write nuance.

cards.lore: Adherence to the rules so absolute it becomes a form of psychological warfare against the audience.
cards.power: Annoy the entire roster into compliance through weaponized purity.

cards.lore: You think you're the hero, but your extremist methods are just villainy with a righteous paint job.
cards.power: Justify extreme, horrific violence by pointing at your shiny 'Good Guy' badge.

cards.lore: You're scared to death, but the script demands you accidentally do the right thing eventually.
cards.power: Extract maximum audience tension by refusing to do your job until the last possible second.

cards.lore: You are considered a hero not because it's right, but because it aligns with your personal grift.
cards.power: Hijack the narrative's moral high ground while maintaining entirely selfish motivations.

cards.lore: "I am on the right side, therefore anything I do to you is mathematically incapable of being wrong."
cards.power: Immune to moral criticism. Reality warps to justify your actions.

cards.lore: Incapable of feeling compassion, leaving you completely unburdened by the pesky rules of the kayfabe.
cards.power: Bypass all Moral Dilemma cards. Empathy is a mechanic for weaker players.

cards.lore: You have absolutely no traces of evil in you, making you an incredibly boring liability to the team.
cards.power: Instantly trigger the "Protect the Mascot" objective for all nearby players.

cards.lore: You're a villain who forgot to pack traditional evil qualities, relying entirely on aesthetic brooding.
cards.power: Confuse the audience into rooting against the actual heroes.

cards.lore: The designated character whose sole job is to act as an un-ignorable, highly annoying moral guideline.
cards.power: Paralyze your tag-team partner with weaponized guilt.

cards.lore: You don't just do immoral acts; you are the merchandising rights for immorality itself.
cards.power: Generate infinite sin tokens to bribe the referee.

cards.lore: Losing your belief in the universe's booking committee instantly transforms you into a top-tier villain.
cards.power: Convert all your collected "Prayers" into "Spite" tokens.

cards.lore: The naive belief that a systemic apex predator wouldn't be so evil if they just had a buddy.
cards.power: Disarm an opponent by forcing a mandatory hug sequence.

cards.lore: You betray your own people by refusing to stick to the demographic the marketing team assigned you.
cards.power: Bypass faction-specific traps by pretending you belong there.

cards.lore: A character seeking to make up for bad deeds, mostly because the consequences finally caught up.
cards.power: Farm unlimited pity from the audience for crimes you already enjoyed committing.

cards.lore: Taking an identity previously used for evil and slapping a fresh coat of "Good" PR on it.
cards.power: Inherit the stats of a dead villain without the moral baggage.

cards.lore: You fought the evil so hard, you accidentally memorized their playbook and started using it.
cards.power: Gain villain abilities, but lose your hero insurance.

cards.lore: You've done too much wrong to ever be forgiven. Welcome to the permanent Heel roster.
cards.power: Permanently lock your alignment to "Unforgivable."

cards.lore: They claim to be your tag partner, but they are just waiting for the referee to look away.
cards.power: Deal double damage during a cooperative tag-team maneuver.

cards.lore: You can never be free of being evil. The universe literally bends to make your hobbies malicious.
cards.power: Automatically fail any redemption arc to retain your cool aesthetic.

cards.lore: You can never abandon somebody in need, making you the easiest mark in the arena.
cards.power: Intercept all incoming damage directed at NPCs, whether you want to or not.

cards.lore: You finally choose a side after realizing the audience was falling asleep.
cards.power: Gain a massive surprise attack bonus against both factions.

cards.lore: Everyone suspects you of being a mastermind, but the horrifying truth is you are exactly as boring as you seem.
cards.power: Immune to all 'Reveal Traitor' mechanics.

cards.lore: An extremely binary moral worldview where anyone slightly disagreeing with you is one-dimensionally evil.
cards.power: Force all gray-area characters to pick a side or take fatal damage.

cards.lore: Morality that's so bizarre, unconventional, and distorted that the referee's brain melts trying to score it.
cards.power: Your actions become completely immune to standard logic checks.

cards.lore: Good and evil must exist in balance, which gives the worst villains endless loopholes to make a grand return.
cards.power: Automatically resurrect the villain if the hero wins too decisively.

cards.lore: Without a heel to fight, the hero loses their merchandising deal. Evil is just job security.
cards.power: Generate profit by keeping the central conflict completely unresolved.

cards.lore: Heroic groups are secretly being managed by the exact villains they are trying to punch.
cards.power: Extract resources from heroic players who think they are saving the world.

cards.lore: The traditionally good, all-knowing force actually hates you and is booking this match for laughs.
cards.power: Rewrite one rule on the board mid-game purely out of spite.

cards.lore: An extremely middle-ground worldview positing that everyone's on the same morally dubious, boring level.
cards.power: Drain all passion and kinetic energy from the current turn.

cards.lore: You're the protagonist, therefore anyone not explicitly clapping for you must be an enemy.
cards.power: Any war crime you commit is automatically reclassified as a "quirky mistake."

cards.lore: The establishment's propaganda that any deviation from their script is a force for ultimate villainy.
cards.power: Destroy the current arena, removing all rules for one turn.

cards.lore: Tradition and rules aren't here to protect you; they're here to make sure you stay in your cubicle.
cards.power: Paralyze an opponent with insurmountable bureaucratic red tape.

cards.lore: You aren't really concerned with good or evil. You just want everyone to know you're smarter than them.
cards.power: Ignore all moral-based attacks because you simply "do not care."

cards.cardName: Sliding Scale of Idealism vs. Cynicism
cards.lore: Optimism and pessimism locked in an eternal, agonizing grappling match.
cards.power: Flip the game's tone: positive effects become negative, and vice versa.

cards.lore: A gratuitously cruel act used when the writer is too lazy to give you actual character development.
cards.power: Generate instant, massive heat from the audience to establish yourself as the Heel.

cards.lore: You're forced to do something horrible for the "greater good," but mostly for the drama.
cards.power: Eliminate a sympathetic character to force the plot forward.

cards.lore: You have a perfectly logical, highly detailed reason for committing blatant theft.
cards.power: Steal an item from another player and successfully argue why it's fair.

cards.lore: Avoiding owning up to your misdeeds through the ultimate superpower: liquid capital.
cards.power: Cancel any incoming punishment by paying double its value in tokens.

cards.lore: Sacrificing one life to save others, usually while looking incredibly brooding and sad about it.
cards.power: Sacrifice a low-tier friendly unit to survive a board-wipe.

cards.lore: Harsh, apocalyptic vengeance for the most petty, mundane slights imaginable.
cards.power: Deal 10x damage in response to being poked.

cards.lore: Doing horrific, mean things is totally justified if the victim was a jerk first.
cards.power: Use villain weapons without taking an alignment penalty.

cards.lore: You'll leave everyone else to die to save your own butt, and you won't even feel bad about it.
cards.power: Sacrifice your tag-team partner to instantly escape the arena.

cards.lore: Letting your enemy live with a Fate Worse Than Death so you can keep your "Hero" rating.
cards.power: Keep an opponent alive but completely remove their ability to play the game.

cards.lore: Stripping away free will is perfectly acceptable as long as it's for a "good cause."
cards.power: Force an opponent's card to permanently fight for you.

cards.cardName: Get Out of Jail Free Card
cards.lore: You cut the villain a break because they are too popular with the fanbase to write out of the story.
cards.power: Automatically cancel any "Arrest" or "Banish" effect.

cards.lore: When moral dilemmas and negotiations get too complicated, just use the easy way out.
cards.power: Ignore all puzzle mechanics and just destroy the target.

cards.lore: You get away scot-free with everything, infuriating the audience and breaking the cosmic scales.
cards.power: Evade all end-of-game consequences regardless of your alignment score.

cards.lore: The universe finally remembers to do its job, and you die as a direct, ironic consequence of your wickedness.
cards.power: Defeat an opponent by letting them trigger their own trap.

cards.lore: After enduring absolute hell, everything works out for you... assuming you survive the trauma.
cards.power: Claim victory, but your character is permanently retired.

cards.lore: Doing good deeds actively backfires, proving the kayfabe is rigged against the pure.
cards.power: Take 2 damage every time you use a "Heal" or "Protect" action.

cards.cardName: Screw the Rules, I Have Money!
cards.lore: Being rich lets you buy a private, luxury box outside of the morality spectrum.
cards.power: Ignore any game rule by paying the bank.

cards.lore: Being rewarded excessively for a minor act of kindness, throwing the entire economy out of balance.
cards.power: Gain massive end-game points for a completely trivial action.

cards.lore: You did the bare minimum of good deeds, and the universe decides to pay out the jackpot.
cards.power: Convert all stored 'Good Karma' directly into win conditions.

cards.lore: After 10 seasons of getting away with it, the writers finally remember you exist and drop the hammer.
cards.power: Instantly delete one specific opponent who has wronged you.
